contract_revision_note: Authoritative spec is CONTRACT-v2.md v2.0 (DRAFT). scenario_version stays 1 on purpose: the compatible_targets / allowed_pairs below are the v1-active comparison set and are NOT asserted to be v2-machine-compliant. Restate (baseline-only) and spring-on-exeris (H1 vs H2C protocol mismatch) are deliberately excluded from comparative rows. No row here asserts v2 correctness-gate compliance; per-section v2 enforcement status is in scenarios/e2e-shop-order-saga/CONTRACT-v2-IMPLEMENTATION.md.

compatible_targets.notes: Comparison-eligible for within-tier H2C (community, loopback-h2c) under required_contract=exeris_community_h2c_v1. No cross-tier inference.
Comparison-eligible for within-tier H2C (community, loopback-h2c) under required_contract=quarkus_axon_neo4j_v1. Axon Framework overhead ~3-5% (documented, expected).
Comparison-eligible for within-tier H2C (community, loopback-h2c) under required_contract=spring_boot_axon_neo4j_v1. Axon Framework + Spring Boot overhead ~4-7% (documented, expected).

framework_difference.baseline_event: Exeris Events L3 with transactional outbox
Exeris Events L3 with transactional outbox

framework_difference.shared_event: Both use Axon Event Sourcing + Outbox

forbidden_pairs.reason: Community vs Enterprise cross-tier — protocol fairness requires separate contracts
Cross-protocol comparisons are out of scope (H1 vs H2C vs H3 must be segregated)
Network-path vs loopback transport modes cannot be compared directly
Cross-backend comparisons are invalid (neo4j vs postgres-graph/pgq)
AGE compatibility runs are not performance-equivalent to PGQ pure runs

cross_tier_equivalence_constraints.concurrency_model: EXACTLY 100 HTTP/2 H2C connections (identical VU thread pool)
cross_tier_equivalence_constraints.payload: EXACTLY identical order JSON schema (order placement endpoint)
cross_tier_equivalence_constraints.protocol: EXACTLY HTTP/2 Cleartext (no TLS cost differential)
cross_tier_equivalence_constraints.database: EXACTLY identical within each comparison track (Track A: PostgreSQL + Neo4j, Track B: PostgreSQL + PGQ)

acceptable_framework_differences.framework_overhead: Exeris Flow (kernel-built) vs Quarkus/Spring Axon Framework
Exeris Graph L2 (native) vs Neo4j Bolt driver (Community)
acceptable_framework_differences.attribution: Graph driver heap allocation and serialization (expected, documented)

acceptable_framework_differences.framework_overhead: Exeris Events L3 (kernel) vs Axon Event Sourcing + Outbox
acceptable_framework_differences.attribution: Event subscription and outbox polling mechanics (expected, documented)

overclaiming_prevention: ALL comparisons MUST include framework overhead caveats
DO NOT claim 'Exeris is X% faster' without acknowledging Axon Framework is a separate system
CORRECT CLAIM: 'E2E order sagas complete X% faster on Exeris native Flow vs Quarkus/Spring + Axon Framework (framework overhead component: ~Y%)'
Include attribution table: saga orchestration overhead (kernel vs framework) + graph driver overhead + event backend overhead
Distinguish between throughput and saga completion latency (different metrics, different claims)
Use 95% CI ranges for all claims; absolute differences require MIN 15% relative separation

must_include: Protocol equivalence table (identical H2C, no TLS)
Payload equivalence attestation (identical order JSON schema)
Concurrency equivalence table (100 VUs, identical thread pool)
Database equivalence attestation (identical PostgreSQL + Neo4j versions)
Saga completion rate by state (COMPLETED, COMPENSATED, FAILED)
Compensation polling statistics (avg polls, max polls, timeout rate)
known asymmetries for query language/planner differences
must_not_include: Absolute claims like 'X% faster' without framework overhead attribution
Cross-protocol comparisons (H1 vs H2C vs H3)
Saga success rate without compensation state breakdown
backend superiority claims from cross-family runs
unqualified percentage speed claims across mixed graph_backend_family
